correctLines: That's going in my good-news update.
wrongLines: That's going in my status report.

characters.introLine: What exactly do we mean by fast?
correctLines: Crystal clear. I'm framing that answer.
That's exactly what the user story meant!
wrongLines: Hmm, that's not what the user story says.
Adding that to my list of questions.

tasks.prompt: The client wants a "small" new feature two days before release. Your first move?

options.text: Say yes to keep them happy
Quietly add it to the sprint
Estimate the impact, then agree a date with the client

tasks.explanation: Surprise scope is risky. Assess the impact and agree a plan before committing.

tasks.prompt: A user story should say who needs something and why, not just what to build.
tasks.explanation: The who and why help the team find the best solution, not just any solution.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this requirement untestable.
tasks.text: The system should load {{fast}} and be {{user-friendly}} for {{most}} users.
tasks.explanation: None of these can be tested without a measurable definition.

tasks.prompt: A sprint goal should be agreed with the team, not just handed to them.
tasks.explanation: Teams commit to goals they helped shape. Handed-down goals rarely stick.

tasks.prompt: Which acceptance criterion is testable?

options.text: Search returns results within 2 seconds for 95% of queries
The form is easy to use

tasks.explanation: Only one option has a measurable target a tester can check.

tasks.prompt: Order these from first to last when kicking off a new project.

items.text: Estimate and plan the first sprint
Break the work into a backlog

tasks.explanation: Goals first, then a backlog, then a sprint plan, then code.

tasks.prompt: Testers should be involved when requirements are written, not only after coding.
tasks.explanation: Early testing questions catch gaps before they become bugs.

tasks.prompt: A stakeholder says: just make it like the old system. What do you ask first?

options.text: Can I have the old system's source code?
When do you need it by?
Which parts of the old system work well for you, and why?

tasks.explanation: Knowing what people value in the old system stops you copying its problems too.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this commitment vague.
tasks.text: We will deliver {{most}} features by {{early}} next quarter
tasks.explanation: Which features, and which date? Commit to specific scope and a specific date.

tasks.prompt: The team is estimating a story nobody fully understands. What should happen?

options.text: Give it a big number and move on
Let the most senior person decide
Run a short spike to learn more first

tasks.explanation: A time-boxed spike turns unknowns into knowledge, so the real estimate means something.

tasks.prompt: Put the parts of this user story in the usual order.

items.text: I want to save my card details

tasks.explanation: User stories follow: As a... I want... So that...

tasks.prompt: Two stakeholders want opposite things from the same feature. What do you do?

options.text: Bring them together to agree on priorities

tasks.explanation: Conflicts are resolved by getting both people in the same room, not by guessing.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words a tester can't verify.
tasks.text: Reports must export {{quickly}} and look {{professional}} in PDF format
tasks.explanation: Quickly and professional need numbers or examples before anyone can test them.

tasks.prompt: Your team's velocity is 30 points. The client wants 45 next sprint. Best response?

options.text: Agree on the most valuable 30 points

tasks.explanation: Plan to real capacity and prioritize. Overcommitting just moves the problem to the end of the sprint.

tasks.prompt: Which commit message is most helpful?

options.text: Fix crash when the cart is empty at checkout

tasks.explanation: Good commit messages say what changed and why, so future readers don't have to guess.

tasks.prompt: Adding more developers to a late project always makes it finish sooner.
tasks.explanation: New people need onboarding and coordination. Adding them late often slows things down.

tasks.prompt: Users aged 18 or over may sign up. What's wrong with this check?
tasks.explanation: The > sign excludes exactly 18. The check needs >= instead.

tasks.prompt: A field accepts ages 18 to 60. Which values test the boundaries best?
tasks.explanation: Bugs cluster at the edges. Test just inside and just outside each limit.

tasks.prompt: Code review is only useful for catching bugs.
tasks.explanation: Reviews also spread knowledge, keep code consistent and help newer teammates learn.

tasks.prompt: A requirement says 'dates' but not which format. What should the developer do?

options.text: Ask the BA and record the answer in the story

tasks.explanation: Clarify, then write it down, so the next person doesn't have to ask again.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this estimate risky.
tasks.explanation: Stacked hedges signal hidden unknowns. Name the risk instead.

tasks.prompt: Mid-sprint, a developer says their task will take twice as long. Best reaction?

options.text: Ask what changed and re-plan together

tasks.explanation: Surprises are information. Understand the cause, then adjust the plan openly.

tasks.prompt: Order these steps for fixing a bug.
tasks.explanation: Reproduce it, capture it in a test, fix it, then prove the fix. The test stops the bug coming back.

tasks.prompt: A developer says: works on my machine. What's the most useful reply?

options.text: Let's compare our environments and steps

tasks.explanation: Differences in data, settings or versions usually explain it. Compare, don't argue.

tasks.prompt: Changing a requirement mid-sprint is fine as long as nobody tells the team.
tasks.explanation: Changes happen, but hidden changes cause rework and broken trust.

tasks.prompt: What's risky about this line?

options.text: A password is written directly in the code
The variable name is too long

tasks.explanation: Secrets in code end up in version control. Keep them in configuration or a secrets store.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this bug report hard to act on.
tasks.text: The app {{sometimes}} crashes when you do {{stuff}} on the screen
tasks.explanation: Developers need exact steps and how often it happens. Sometimes and stuff won't reproduce anything.

tasks.prompt: Two developers disagree on a design in code review. Best next step?

options.text: Discuss the trade-offs, and ask a third person if still stuck

tasks.explanation: Talk through the trade-offs. A fresh pair of eyes breaks ties better than stubbornness.

tasks.prompt: Order these from broadest to most detailed.
tasks.explanation: Epics break into stories, and stories are pinned down by acceptance criteria.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this status update unhelpful.
tasks.text: The build is {{basically}} done and {{mostly}} working now
tasks.explanation: Basically and mostly hide what's left. Say exactly what's done and what isn't.

tasks.prompt: A test suite that passes 100% of the time proves the software has no bugs.
tasks.explanation: Tests only find the bugs they look for. Passing tests reduce risk; they don't prove perfection.

tasks.prompt: What's the most useful title for a bug report?

options.text: Checkout button does nothing on Android when a discount code is applied

tasks.explanation: A good title says what fails, where and when, so anyone can triage it at a glance.

tasks.prompt: This loop should print 1 to 5. What does it actually print?
tasks.explanation: i < 5 stops before 5. It needs i <= 5.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that need a number before this can be built.
tasks.text: Show a warning when the balance is {{low}} for {{several}} days
tasks.explanation: How low, and how many days? Without numbers, every developer will pick their own.

tasks.prompt: A bug fix is ready at 4:55 pm on Friday. The release is Monday. What's wisest?

options.text: Merge it, test it, and ship with Monday's release
Deploy it without tests to save time

tasks.explanation: Friday-evening deploys leave nobody around to fix surprises. Test it and ship on the plan.

tasks.prompt: Order these tests from fastest to slowest to run.
tasks.explanation: Unit tests take milliseconds, integration tests seconds, end-to-end tests longest. That's why the test pyramid has so many unit tests.

tasks.prompt: The daily standup keeps running for 40 minutes. What's the best fix?

options.text: Take detailed discussions offline after the standup
Make everyone stand on one leg

tasks.explanation: Standups are for syncing. Problem-solving happens afterward with just the people who need it.

tasks.prompt: Tap the vague words in this pull request description.
tasks.text: Made {{some}} changes to {{things}} in the login code
tasks.explanation: Reviewers need to know what changed and why. Some things tells them nothing.

tasks.prompt: The team keeps building the wrong thing. Which practice helps most?

options.text: Reviewing small increments with users often

tasks.explanation: Frequent feedback on small pieces catches misunderstandings while they're cheap to fix.

tasks.prompt: You find the same 20 lines of code copied in five places. What's best?

options.text: Move it into one shared function

tasks.explanation: One shared function means one place to fix bugs instead of five.

tasks.prompt: A login button that's two pixels off is a release blocker.
tasks.explanation: Cosmetic issues rarely block a release.

tasks.prompt: Which bug should be fixed first?

options.text: A typo on the About page
Users can see other users' invoices
An old logo in the footer

tasks.explanation: A data leak hurts privacy and trust. It beats every cosmetic or speed issue.

tasks.prompt: Testing finds a serious bug the day before release. What do you do?

options.text: Assess the risk with the team and decide to fix or delay, openly
Release anyway and hope nobody notices

tasks.explanation: Make the call with facts and tell stakeholders. Hidden bugs become public incidents.

tasks.prompt: Order these bugs from most to least severe.

items.text: Export fails in Firefox, works in Chrome

tasks.explanation: A blocker beats a broken feature with a workaround, which beats slowness, which beats a cosmetic issue.

tasks.prompt: A tester and a developer read the same acceptance criterion differently. What fixes it?

options.text: Rewrite the criterion with a concrete example

tasks.explanation: Examples remove ambiguity. Given, When, Then with real values leaves nothing to interpret.

tasks.prompt: Exploratory testing means clicking around randomly with no goal.
tasks.explanation: Good exploratory testing has a mission and a time box, and testers learn as they go.

tasks.prompt: A test fails randomly about once in ten runs. What should the team do?

options.text: Investigate it as a real bug in the test or the code

tasks.explanation: Flaky tests hide real problems and teach everyone to ignore failures. Find the cause.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this test case unrepeatable.
tasks.text: Enter {{some}} data and check it looks {{right}}
tasks.explanation: Test cases need exact inputs and expected results, so anyone gets the same outcome.

tasks.prompt: If testers find lots of bugs, the testers are doing a bad job.
tasks.explanation: Finding bugs before users do is exactly the job.

tasks.prompt: What's the difference between severity and priority?

options.text: Severity is set by managers only
Severity is the impact; priority is how soon to fix it
Priority is how many users complain

tasks.explanation: A typo on the home page can be low severity but high priority. They answer different questions.

tasks.prompt: Order the parts of this test scenario.

items.text: Then they see: Your cart is empty
Given a user with an empty cart

tasks.explanation: Given sets the scene, When is the action, Then is the expected result.

tasks.prompt: A fix is ready for a bug you reported. What do you test?

options.text: Only the exact steps in the bug report
The fix, plus nearby features it could affect

tasks.explanation: Confirm the fix, then check its neighbors. Fixes often break something next door.

tasks.prompt: Tap the words that make this test result unclear.
tasks.text: Checkout {{seems}} to work but looks {{odd}} on phones
tasks.explanation: Report facts: what you did, what you expected and what you saw.

tasks.prompt: Order these environments from first to last on a typical release path.
tasks.explanation: Code moves from a laptop through shared test environments to staging. Production comes last.

tasks.prompt: Release notes should list the known issues that are still open.
tasks.explanation: Being upfront about known issues builds trust and saves support time.

tasks.prompt: The release just went live. What should testers check first?

options.text: Quick smoke tests of the most important user journeys

tasks.explanation: Smoke tests confirm the critical paths work in production before anything else.

tasks.prompt: After release, users use a feature differently than planned. Best next step?

options.text: Tell users they're doing it wrong
Ignore it, the spec was right
Learn why, and feed it into the next requirements

tasks.explanation: Real usage beats assumptions. Treat it as research for the next iteration.

tasks.prompt: Feature flags let you deploy code without switching the feature on for users.
tasks.explanation: Flags separate deploying from releasing, so features can be switched on gradually or off quickly.

tasks.prompt: Order these release-day steps.
tasks.explanation: Approve, deploy, check it works, then tell the world. Announcing before smoke tests invites embarrassment.

tasks.prompt: Users report a problem nobody can reproduce. What's the best next step?

options.text: Close it as works for me
Ask for details like device, steps and time, and check the logs

tasks.explanation: Missing context is usually the difference. Gather details and check the logs before giving up.

tasks.prompt: After go-live, a minor bug appears and users are asking about it. Best move?

options.text: Acknowledge it and share a workaround and a fix date

tasks.explanation: Honest, quick communication keeps trust. A minor bug rarely needs a full rollback.

tasks.prompt: Bugs found in production should be turned into regression tests.
tasks.explanation: A test for every escaped bug stops it sneaking back in a later release.

tasks.prompt: A release needs a database change. What's the safest approach?

options.text: Change the live database by hand
A scripted migration that's tested before release
Copy the database into a spreadsheet

tasks.explanation: Scripted, tested migrations are repeatable and reviewable. Manual changes are how data goes missing.

tasks.prompt: What's the best way to tell whether a new feature succeeded?

options.text: Check whether it moved its goal, like fewer support calls
Measure how long it took to build
Count the meetings that discussed it

tasks.explanation: Success is measured by outcomes for users and the business, not by effort or output.

tasks.prompt: Order these steps in a bug's life.

items.text: Log the bug with clear steps

tasks.explanation: Log it, fix it, retest it, then close it. Closing before retesting is how bugs come back.

tasks.prompt: At the last minute, a stakeholder asks for the release a bit earlier. Best reply?

options.text: Agree, then miss the date anyway
Explain what would be cut or risked, and let them choose

tasks.explanation: Make the trade-off visible. Earlier dates cost scope or quality, and the stakeholder should choose which.

tasks.prompt: A feature is only done when it meets its acceptance criteria.
tasks.explanation: Acceptance criteria are the agreed finish line. Without them, done means different things to different people.

tasks.prompt: The release is done. When should the team hold a retrospective?

options.text: Soon, while details are fresh, whether it went well or badly
Never, retros are a waste of time

tasks.explanation: Retros find what to keep as well as what to fix, and memories fade fast.

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: what does QA stand for?
tasks.explanation: Just practice. Good luck in the real round!

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: a sprint usually lasts between one and four weeks.
tasks.explanation: Just practice.

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: put these in delivery order.
tasks.explanation: Just practice.

tasks.prompt: Warm-up: tap the two fruits.
tasks.text: The developer ate an {{apple}} and a {{banana}} before standup.
tasks.explanation: Just practice.

tasks.prompt: Production is down right after the 5 pm deploy. What do you do first?

options.text: Roll back to the last good release
Push a quick patch without testing

tasks.explanation: Restore service first, investigate afterward.

tasks.prompt: Customers can see other customers' orders after this morning's release. First move?

options.text: Wait to see if anyone complains
Add a disclaimer to the page
Take the feature offline and alert the security team
Schedule a meeting for next week

tasks.explanation: A data leak is an emergency. Stop the exposure first, then investigate and inform the right people.
